subject: Archaeology
title: Astronomy in Babylon
description: A 60-second lesson on Astronomy in Babylon.

hook.text: Babylonian priests tracked the stars so precisely that they predicted eclipses centuries before the Greeks even tried.

buildup.text: Astronomical diaries recorded planetary positions nightly for over 700 years — the longest continuous scientific record.

discovery.text: The MUL.APIN tablets listed constellations, rising times, and seasonal markers that farmers and priests relied on.

twist.text: The zodiac — Aries, Taurus, Gemini — is a Babylonian invention. Greek astrology copied it almost directly.

climax.text: A 2016 study found Babylonians used geometric methods to track Jupiter — predating European calculus by 1,400 years.

punchline.text: Your horoscope sign was named by Babylonian priests.

quiz.question: What groundbreaking mathematical method did Babylonian astronomers use?
options: They invented the telescope to observe the planets more closely
They used geometric methods to track Jupiter, predating European calculus by 1,400 years
They developed a heliocentric model of the solar system
